structured_output.question: Why did narrowing only the first stage (128->96 channels at 32x32, directly after the frozen 2x2 patch-whitening layer) cost ~0.5 pp of CIFAR-100 accuracy at 11 epochs (E019: 0.7515 vs E012: 0.7567) while saving only ~10% of wall time? Is early-stage width a sample-efficiency (optimization-speed) bottleneck rather than a capacity one in short training: for example, through a rank or information bottleneck right after whitening, slower feature learning in narrow early layers, or width-dependent effective learning rate under SGD with BN? Given a fixed FLOP or time budget, how should width be split across stages (stage 1 vs 2 vs 3) for short-schedule, many-class CNN training? This decides whether the remaining width cuts (block 3, or block 2 below 256) are worth trying, or whether FLOPs should instead go back into stage 1 while other stages are cut.

rubric: Reports how accuracy changes when width is varied per stage or per layer (not only uniform width scaling) for CNNs on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet or similar, ideally at a fixed FLOP or time budget.
Addresses short or compute-limited training (few epochs, time-to-accuracy, speedruns), or separates width's effect on optimization speed and sample efficiency from its effect on final capacity.

Gives a mechanism or quantitative rule (e.g. a sensitivity ranking of stages, an optimal width ratio, or a rank/information bottleneck after the stem) that can be tested by changing stage widths in a 3-stage VGG-style net with BN.
Trains from scratch, with no pretrained weights or distillation from external teachers.
exclude: Methods requiring pretrained weights, transfer learning, or external/extra data
Knowledge distillation from a pretrained teacher
Test-time augmentation or any use of the test set for tuning
Pruning methods that require first training the full network to convergence (prune-after-train) without from-scratch width findings
Transformer/ViT-only or NLP-only width scaling studies
Neural architecture search requiring large GPU-day searches with no transferable width rule
